exposure: bushfire late pregnancy, born before lockdown
bushfires in early-mid pregnancy, born during lockdown or soon after
conceived during bushfires, lockdown in second trimester
conceived after bushfires, pregnancy during restrictions
cohort: 60,054 pregnant women who gave birth in South Sydney between November 2017 and December 2020
finding: Pregnancies exposed to both severe climate events (bushfires) and pandemic disruptions (COVID-19 lockdown) appear to have an increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes compared to experiencing only one event.
mod_finding: Exposure to bushfires in early-mid pregnancy was associated with an increase in prelabor rupture of membranes and cesarean sections, while conception during bushfires and lockdown in the second trimester was associated with an increase in unplanned cesarean sections.
